> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b88c356413a6e9f66ae4eba50b46003ad6895081` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cc6fc5f1f67d54b79a2d518c53c97735afc31a81` — the merge of head `fca16e06887636ff4301efcc40643619db17bb40` into base `b88c356413a6e9f66ae4eba50b46003ad6895081`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cc6fc5f1f67d54b79a2d518c53c97735afc31a81 && git checkout cc6fc5f1f67d54b79a2d518c53c97735afc31a81
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b88c356413a6e9f66ae4eba50b46003ad6895081 fca16e06887636ff4301efcc40643619db17bb40 && git checkout -B drift-repro b88c356413a6e9f66ae4eba50b46003ad6895081 && git merge --no-ff fca16e06887636ff4301efcc40643619db17bb40

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b88c356413a6e9f66ae4eba50b46003ad6895081
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b88c356413a6e9f66ae4eba50b46003ad6895081` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fca16e06887636ff4301efcc40643619db17bb40`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #22019 (body; comments 6021332805, 6021803960, 6023710038), PR #22031 (body, file list, net diff against the merge base 299a2c624c), the 35 check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run. The dispatch order and the dispatching seat's conclusions were not read as inputs.

Check-runs on the head: every required context is `success` (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Temporal Conformance, Governed Surface Queue Guard). Check Changeset, the claim gates and the single-writer-path gate are `success`. Three jobs are `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke), all path-filtered or opt-in. No failures. The PR touches 9 files, 772 added and 50 removed, none on a governed surface. It is a draft and auto-merge is not armed.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept set.**

1. An object write in publish mode whose `fields[].expression` the shared validator refuses answered 200 and now answers 422 `INVALID_METADATA` with an `expression-invalid` issue located at `object 'NAME' · field 'FIELD' expression`. Right. The cause is one declaration: `runtimeTypes` on the `validateStackExpressions` entry gains `'object'` (packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts:602). The gate reads that list and nothing else (packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts:550-554). Stated in `.changeset/22019-object-save-door-formula-verdict.md`.
2. A formula the build only warns on still saves. Right. `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` splits findings by severity (runtime-gate.ts:1006-1008). `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` returns `error: null` when `errors` is empty (packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts:1134). The warnings ride the existing `advisories` key. The unprovisioned-anchor warning rides the same way (validate-expressions.ts:1266-1290, called at :1968). Stated in the changeset.
3. Draft saves are unchanged. The gate returns before any rule on a draft (protocol.ts:6125; runtime-authoring-gate.ts:1037). Right.
4. Flow, action and hook writes are unchanged. The fence keys on one comparison, `options.runtimeWriteType === 'object'` (validate-expressions.ts:1228). Any other write type runs every pass as before. Pinned: `runtime-gate.object-formula-writes.test.ts`, the test "a flow write still runs every pass it ran". Right.
5. The CLI commands are unchanged. `runAuthoringRules` builds a context with no `runtimeWriteType` (authoring-rules.ts:2138-2142). `validateStackExpressions(stack)` passes `{}` (validate-expressions.ts:1209-1211). The entry runs on all three commands (`commands: ALL`, authoring-rules.ts:539). The formula pass is a closure called at the same point of the field walk the removed inline block sat at (head :2116, base :2020-2054), so finding order is unchanged. Right.
6. The read answer is unchanged. On a fault `rec[fp.name] = null` as before (packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:2272-2273). What is new is the sink call on the next line (:2274). Right.
7. The read-path log: one `warn` per (object, field) per engine instance, through the engine's logger. `reportFormulaFault` keys a per-instance `Set` on `[object, field]` (engine.ts:5146-5149) and writes through `this.logger.warn` (:5153), the `Logger` bound from the host context (:3693, :3829). The sink is bound at `find` (:12150), `findOne` (:12426), the insert response (:13890) and the update response (:15684). Level `warn` is right by AGENTS.md's one question: nothing persisted is lost and the `null` is visible to the reader. The runtime string carries no tracker number. Pinned in `engine-formula-fault-log.test.ts` (six cases, including once-per-instance). Right.
8. One `applyFormulaPlan` call stays unbound: `evaluateFormulaField` (engine.ts:2384-2393), the hook-side helper with no engine, still answers `null` with no line. Disclosed in `.changeset/22019-objectql-formula-fault-log.md`. Judged under ③.

**The fence.** I read every loop in `runStackExpressionPasses` (validate-expressions.ts:1222-2258). The top-level passes are flows (:1514), validation rules (:1859), the field-slot passes (:1971-1976, which `continue` after the formula pass on an object write), stack actions (:2166), object actions (:2169), sharing rules (:2183) and hooks (:2198). Each reads an empty list under `fieldFormulasOnly`. The loop at :1241 builds the unprovisioned-anchor index and emits nothing. The stretch :1900-1970 defines holders and the `judgeFieldFormula` closure and emits nothing. On an object write the only emitter is `judgeFieldFormula` (:1957-1968): the validator's errors, its warnings, and the anchor warning. The gate is the only setter of `runtimeWriteType` (runtime-gate.ts:979), so no other pass can reach the object door without an edit to this function, and that edit is pinned: the fence block of `runtime-gate.object-formula-writes.test.ts` puts a fault in each fenced pass, the build flags every one, the object door flags none. The build's own entry is unchanged: every pass runs at build (judgment 5). Right.

**Door verdict equals build verdict.** Both doors run the same entry `run` mapping to rule, where, path, message and hint (authoring-rules.ts:603-611). The gate's `toIssue` copies those five keys and severity (runtime-authoring-gate.ts:841-848). `nameKeyFindingPath` rewrites only positional paths (runtime-gate.ts:991-996); this rule's path is the prose `where`, so it is not rewritten. Pinned key by key against `runAuthoringRules('build', …)` in `protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts`, block "(d)", and in the lint PARITY test. Right.

**Same gate for save, draft promotion and package publish.** `saveMetaItem` calls `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` (protocol.ts:20410). `publishMetaItem` calls `promoteDraftForPublish` (:21690), which calls the same method (:21973). `publishPackageDrafts` calls `promoteDraftForPublish` per draft (:23057) with its batch as `pending`. All reach `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` (protocol.ts:6243; runtime-authoring-gate.ts:897), then `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` (runtime-gate.ts:917), then `runtimeAuthoringRulesFor` (:550). Pinned through the real `saveMetaItem` and `publishMetaItem` in the (a) cases. Right.

**Object write paths that do not run the gate.** All pre-existing and none introduced here: a draft save (protocol.ts:6125, D1); the `package-author` channel (:6124); `source: 'migrate-stored'` (:6140); `OS_ALLOW_UNLINTED_METADATA_WRITES=1`, which logs the refusal and allows the write (runtime-authoring-gate.ts:117, :1177-1188); `rollbackMetaItem` (protocol.ts:25464, `repo.restoreVersion` at :25597) and `revertCommit` (:24803, `repo.restoreVersion` at :25201), which restore a stored version's body with no gate call. The two restore paths are stored-row restores under the gate's D4 asymmetry and predate this PR for all ten object-gated rules. Not this PR's defect. Noted for the seat.

**Public surface.** `@objectstack/lint`: `validateStackExpressions(stack)` keeps its signature (validate-expressions.ts:1209). `runStackExpressionPasses` and `StackExpressionOptions` are module exports that `index.ts` does not re-export (index.ts:66-67 export only `validateStackExpressions`, `fieldRuleRootIssue`, `FIELD_RULE_BOUND_ROOTS` and the `ExprIssue` type) and `runtime.ts` does not touch. `AuthoringRuleContext.runtimeWriteType` gains a doc comment only (authoring-rules.ts:309-314). The object door roster grows by one rule, pinned (`runtime-gate.object-writes.test.ts:114-120, :400`). `@objectstack/objectql`: three private members on `ObjectQL`; `applyFormulaPlan` and `hydrateWriteFormulas` are module-private and gain an optional trailing parameter. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: no source change; the door's behaviour arrives through the lint dist it already consumes (`workspace:*`). All right as the PR body states.

### ② Semver level

Two changesets, both added by this PR.

`.changeset/22019-object-save-door-formula-verdict.md`: `@objectstack/lint: minor`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`, title `fix(lint)!:`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, a BREAKING section with a remedy, an ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.

- Level. The repo versions every published package in one `fixed` group (`.changeset/config.json`), at the highest level found. A `minor` on lint alone bumps metadata-protocol identically. Naming metadata-protocol moves no version; it places the BREAKING text in metadata-protocol's CHANGELOG, which is where the 422 is met (`saveMetaItem`, `publishMetaItem`, REST `PUT /meta/object`). That is the right placement, and the dev disclosed it (6023710038, deviations, third entry). No gate forbids naming a package the diff does not touch; `check-changeset-no-major`'s level axis is satisfied by lint, whose published source moves. Moving the entry to lint alone would lose the CHANGELOG placement for no version effect. Judged right.
- `minor` for a narrowing. The launch-window convention grades breaking as `minor`, with the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition as the carriers (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` header). Both carriers are present.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Clause ② means a new key on a published payload (check-changeset-no-major.mjs:7). This diff adds none: the 422's `issues[]` and `rulesRun`, and the 2xx `advisories`, all pre-exist. The accept set narrows. The form matches AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3: `no` with the `(narrowing)` arm is BREAKING. The PR body carries the same line. The claim's provisional reading (6021803960) was measured and kept. Right.
- ADR-0087 marker. The category is one of the five the gate knows (check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:495-499) and parses (:1938). Its honesty condition is that the body carries no migration prescription in arrow or table form (:147-154). The Remedy is prose: edit the expression as the located message says, use a function `introspectScope` lists (exists, packages/formula/src/validate.ts:1040), qualify reads as `record.FIELD`, keep a draft, or set the hatch. No authorable key, export or stored shape moves, and no stored row is converted. The Check Changeset check-run, which runs this gate (`.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml:979-980`), is `success`. Right.
- Remedy. Names the fix, the escape (`mode: 'draft'`) and the migration hatch, and states what stays unchanged. Adequate.

`.changeset/22019-objectql-formula-fault-log.md`: `@objectstack/objectql: patch`. A fix; no public surface moves (three private members). Right.

Corpus. The changeset states the measured scope as "every formula field this repository ships", 29 fields on 28 objects, with the split (examples 7 on 6, platform `display_title` 22 on 22). The PR body (H4) and the report (6023710038, `tests`) tie the reading to head `fca16e0688`. The changeset states the unmeasured case by behaviour: a stored body keeps reading until next saved, is judged at that save, and the remedy is given. I searched AGENTS.md, `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`, the pm-dispatch skill and its references, and ADR-0087 for a convention requiring a changeset to declare an out-of-tree census; I found none. The nearest rule is AGENTS.md's reading rule (a count plus repository and commit). The changeset meets it by count and repository; the commit is the changeset's own. Non-blocking: the counts in the authoring-rules.ts:594-600 comment carry no sha, in the same form as the prior crossing's comment at :575-578, so this is repo practice. The triage stop condition (6021332805: stop if stored formula fields in this tree fail the validator) was not triggered: 0 refusals.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6023710038, `deviations`, each answered:

1. Landing in `packages/lint`, not `packages/metadata-protocol`. Answered, accepted. The claim (6021803960) set the landing at "the runtime authoring gate, or wherever `saveMetaItem` judges an object body. The dev measures where", and forbade a new rule or refusal code. `saveMetaItem` judges through the gate, and the gate dispatches the lint registry (protocol.ts:20410 → runtime-authoring-gate.ts:897 → runtime-gate.ts:917, :550). The wiring ratchet (`packages/lint/src/authoring-rule-wiring.test.ts`) requires every surface to consume the table rather than a list of its own, so the registry declaration is the only landing the measurement allows. No new rule (`validateStackExpressions` existed) and no new code (`EXPRESSION_INVALID`, authoring-rules.ts:522, existed). This is the producer-side fix the order allowed. The dispatch reports a late cross-lane declaration on #6017 (6023749907); it is not an input here and was not read. The serial-constraint check-runs are `success` ("No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path"; "The card this PR closes must claim this branch"). 2. The narrowing travels through `AuthoringRuleContext.runtimeWriteType`, and its doc now names this second reader (authoring-rules.ts:309-314). Answered, accepted: the gate is the only setter (runtime-gate.ts:979), and the argument is the one the doc already made for the reference-integrity suite.
3. The metadata-protocol changeset entry names a package with no source change. Answered under ②: accepted.
4. The door pins live in the existing `protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts` to reuse the pinned engine double. Answered, accepted: the block (test:1595-1724) is self-contained and runs the real `saveMetaItem` and `publishMetaItem`.
5. Extra reverse verification for the read-path sink. Answered: noted; nothing was re-run here.
6. One errant build invocation with no code effect. Answered: no carrier.
7. Attribution. The branch's commits end with `Claude-Session` and `Co-authored-by: Claude` trailers (git log on `pr/22031`), and the PR body ends with the session-URL footer. Matches AGENTS.md. Answered.

Answered: a comment correction, not a defect or a contract line; no carrier required under Prime Directive #10.
3. `evaluateFormulaField` still answers `null` with no line. It is reached from the hook sandbox (`packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts:245, :263`) through `resolveRecordTitle` (`packages/objectql/src/record-title.ts:138`). Disclosed in the objectql changeset. Answered, not blocking: the helper has no engine and so no logger, and the same (object, field) pair is reported by the engine on any `find`, `findOne` or write response of that object. The card's "Done when" names the engine read path (`applyFormulaPlan`), which is covered. Left with the seat: a follow-up card is warranted only if ADR-0032 parity is wanted on the hook-side leg.
4. The comment at `protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts:366` says "ALL SEVEN" object-gated rules; the roster is ten. Answered: stale count, no carrier.

`open_questions`: none (6023710038). Nothing to escalate.
